key_insight: LLMs can recognize updated medical guidance without fully incorporating it into their recommendations.
clinical_relevance: Recognition of guideline updates alone may not ensure that clinical LLM recommendations avoid outdated guidance.
method: Introduced ChronoEvo with 1,709 recommendation-level revisions across 12 types of medical knowledge change.
Evaluated recognition and incorporation across 14 models, with two-clinician adjudication of 300 responses.
Tested an intervention that emphasized guideline revisions.
evidence_signal: The primary model recognized 90.8% of revisions but fully incorporated only 58.5%, a 32.3-percentage-point gap; clinician validation found a 40.3-point gap.
watch_item: Emphasizing revisions improved clinical correctness and reduced outdated-content retention but did not significantly improve full incorporation.
paper_title: Large language models show systematic failures in incorporating evolving medical knowledge
